observation_summary: The compiler incorrectly folds array access expressions by removing elements that contain side effects, leading to incorrect program transformation and potential runtime errors when those side effects are expected to execute.
reasoning_summary: The bug report explicitly states that 'tryFoldArrayAccess in com.google.javascript.jscomp.PeepholeFoldConstants should check whether every array element that is not going to be preserved has no side effects.' This indicates that the logic for folding array access is missing a necessary validation check (a guard) to ensure that elements with side effects are not discarded during the optimization process. This fits the definition of a Checking defect.
evidence_used: The bug report description states: 'tryFoldArrayAccess in com.google.javascript.jscomp.PeepholeFoldConstants should check whether every array element that is not going to be preserved has no side effects.'
The failing test 'testFoldGetElem' indicates an unexpected error related to array indexing, which is a consequence of the compiler's incorrect optimization logic.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the folding logic is part of an algorithm, the specific root cause identified is the absence of a side-effect check (a guard) before performing the fold, which is more precisely classified as Checking.
